business_scope.primary_industry_name: Financial Market News Aggregation and Syndication Feed

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.210-1 et seq. and L.227-1 to L.227-30 (SAS); Decree No. 2007-431 as amended.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce maintaining the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); submissions are made through the INPI-operated Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de création d'entreprise (M0 form) filed through the Guichet Unique, together with the signed articles of association (statuts) and all applicable annexes.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum capital for an SAS; capital is freely fixed in the articles. Cash contributions must be paid up to at least 50% at incorporation, with the balance within five years. Cash funds are deposited temporarily in a bank or with the Caisse des Dépôts and released only after RCS registration; no escrow is statutorily mandated for ordinary cash. In-kind contributions must be fully released and valued by a commissaire aux apports when required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: The shareholders of the SAS approve the incorporation of the company under the French Commercial Code, with the corporate name, registered office, corporate object, and share capital as stated in the signed articles of association. The capital is hereby fully subscribed and accepted, in cash and in kind as applicable. RESOLVED FURTHER: The registered office at [address], France, is adopted for the company and registered with the RCS. RESOLVED FINALLY: [Name] is appointed President, with sole authority to direct day-to-day operations, open bank accounts, sign contracts, and exercise the powers conferred by Article L.227-6 of the Code de commerce; [Name] is appointed auditor where required. All necessary filings are authorized.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of articles of association and initial capital collection
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (INPI portal) for the filing module; notarial or private deed preparation as applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the SAS articles including corporate name, registered office address, corporate object (financial market news aggregation, syndicated newswire and API feed), share capital, duration, governance rules and president nomination. Cash capital is subscribed and at least 50% of each cash share must be paid at incorporation. Deposit the funds in a temporary blocked account with a bank or the Caisse des Dépôts. If an in-kind contribution exceeds 30,000 EUR or represents more than half of the capital, have a commissaire aux apports prepare a valuation report. Sign the statuts as an acte sous seing privé unless a notarial deed is required due to a real-property contribution.
required_dossiers: Draft or final signed articles of association
Identity documents of all shareholders
Bank certificate of temporary deposit of cash capital
In-kind contribution valuation report, if applicable
Draft declaration of beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry or notary identifies legal or typographical defects, amend the draft statuts, re-sign the corrected version and restart the formalities before submission to the Guichet Unique.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the statutory legal notice in an approved legal gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) legally authorised for the judicial district of the registered office, e.g. Affiches Parisiennes for Paris.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish the mandatory legal notice containing the corporate form (SAS), corporate name, registered office, share capital, corporate purpose, duration, and identification of the first president. Obtain the attestation de parution from the gazette and preserve it as part of the RCS filing. The publication should occur before the electronic submission of the incorporation dossier.
required_dossiers: Final text of the legal notice
Authority from the incorporators to publish
Copy of draft statuts for gazette verification, if requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the legal gazette rejects the notice or the public prosecutor objects, correct the wording or include omitted mandatory disclosures, republish, and obtain a new attestation de parution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic submission of the incorporation dossier via the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises, operated by the INPI (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online business-creation declaration (M0) and upload the signed statuts, legal publication attestation, capital deposit certificate, registered-office occupancy evidence, declarations of non-conviction for directors, identification documents, and the beneficial-owner declaration. Pay any invoiced registry or greffe fee, and monitor the file until the Guichet closes. The dossier is transmitted electronically to the RCS, INSEE, and competent social and tax administrations.
required_dossiers: Signed statuts
Attestation de parution from the legal gazette
Certificat de dépôt de fonds (capital deposit certificate)
Justificatif de jouissance du siège social (lease, ownership deed, or domiciliation agreement)
Declaration of non-conviction of the president and managers
Valid identity documents of the president and shareholders
Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs (DBE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Guichet issues a demand for complementary documents, cure the omission within 15 calendar days on the same file. If the dossier is rejected, prepare a corrected e-file and resubmit; a judicial challenge may also be brought before the juge de l'immatriculation or the competent civil court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration and issuance of the K-bis extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the competent judicial district (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the Guichet Unique transmission, the greffe checks the legality of the statuts, verifies the company name against conflicting registered names, and records the company in the RCS. Once registered, the company receives SIREN, SIRET, APE code 6391Z and the K-bis extract as conclusive proof of legal personality. The K-bis must be kept at the registered office and provided to business counterparties upon request.
required_dossiers: Transmitted file from Guichet Unique; no separate registry filing is required
Copy of the legal publication attestation (already included in the dossier)
Registered office occupancy evidence (already included)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the greffe requests corrections, comply through the Guichet Unique; if registration is refused, file an application with the supervisory judge (juge de l'immatriculation), who may order inscription under Article R.123-92 of the Code de commerce.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Beneficial-ownership filing and maintenance of corporate statutory registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS) for the beneficial-owner declaration; company registered office for statutory books.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the declaration of beneficial owners is lodged as part of the incorporation file or, where necessary, completed through the RCS electronic interface. Establish and keep the register of share transfers and corporate minutes, record the identity and holdings of each shareholder and beneficial owner, and institute an internal AML-compliant client-intake policy proportional to the low-risk financial newswire activity. Changes in presidents, auditors, or beneficial owners are reported to the RCS within 30 days.
required_dossiers: Beneficial-owner identification and control-chain structure
K-bis extract
Register of share movements (registre des mouvements de titres)
Minute book for shareholders' and board resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the beneficial-owner declaration is queried, submit the corrected information immediately and before any 30-day deadline; late regularization may be accepted with a spontaneous rectification letter, and a refusal can be challenged under RCS supervisory review procedures.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable; DREAL (Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement) would be the competent authority only if future operations trigger ICPE thresholds.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sectoral operating licence required for ISIC 6391 financial newswire aggregation in France; RCS registration with APE code 6391Z and standard employer registrations are sufficient.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition écologique / DREAL
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no EIA is required under Article R.122-2 of the Code de l'environnement for an office-based data aggregation and API service; no ICPE (Installation Classée pour la Protection de l'Environnement) rubric is reached.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or combustion emissions from the newswire activity. Electronic waste, including IT servers and end-user equipment, must be handled under Articles R.543-195 and R.543-202 of the Code de l'environnement. If diesel generators or fuel tanks are installed, applicable DREAL threshold requirements for fuel storage and emergency generators must be observed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Standard office occupancy compliance is required under the Code de la construction and the Code du travail. This includes a fire-safety certificate for any building receiving employees or the public, electrical installation verification, sanitary and accessibility checks, and visible emergency instructions. No separate fire-brigade licence is required for low-capacity office premises; where an établissement recevant du public exceeds 300 persons, prior fire-safety commission approval may be required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), Ministry of Economy, Finance and Industrial Sovereignty; portal: impots.gouv.fr. For non-established foreign entities, the relevant VAT registration service is the Service des Impôts des Entreprises Étrangères (SIEE).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: SAS established in France: incorporate via the online Guichet Unique (guichet-entreprises.fr) with articles of association, registered office details, and president/shareholder information; obtain RCS registration with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; INSEE/DGFiP then allocates SIREN, SIRET, and the intra-Community French VAT number (FR + two-digit key + SIREN). Foreign non-established entity supplying taxable services in France: register directly for VAT with DGFiP/SIEE through the dedicated online teleprocedure on impots.gouv.fr; provide constitutional documents, foreign tax registration proof, expected turnover, business activity description, and, if outside the EU, appoint a French tax representative where required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election and no fiscal pass-through election exists for a French SAS; an SAS is compulsorily subject to entity-level corporation tax (impôt sur les sociétés). Hybrid mismatch rules under Article 212 quinquies and related provisions of the CGI are mandatory, not elective. The only relevant elective corporate tax mechanism is French tax consolidation ('intégration fiscale') available to a 95% French parent, plus the separate authorization regime for worldwide/consolidated profits under Articles 209 quinquies and 209 sexies of the CGI.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: French Value Added Tax (TVA - Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée), governed by Articles 256 to 289 of the Code Général des Impôts (CGI).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: France generally applies no turnover threshold for VAT registration of a non-established foreign supplier; any taxable supply made in France triggers registration unless covered by the EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS) mechanism (distance sales threshold EUR 10,000). For small established French businesses, the French 'franchise en base' applies: EUR 85,000 turnover for goods and EUR 37,500 for services, with safeguards for digital services and occasional transactions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France will require structured electronic invoicing under the réforme de la facturation électronique: domestic B2B invoices must be transmitted through the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) or a certified Partner Dematerialization Platform (PDP) using Factur-X, UBL, or CII formats, phased from 1 September 2026, with small and micro enterprises from 1 September 2027. There is no real-time tax-authority clearance or digital stamping; e-reporting (API-based reporting to DGFiP) is required for B2C and cross-border transactions not covered by e-invoicing.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports outside the EU are taxable at 0% under CGI Article 262-I where the goods physically leave the EU and the supplier retains satisfactory proof of export. Services directly related to exported movable property may be exempt under Article 262-II. For the target financial-newswire API business, French VAT is normally excluded by place-of-supply rules: B2B supplies to a taxable customer established outside France are taxable in the customer's jurisdiction (reverse charge for EU customers; outside French VAT for non-EU customers); B2C digital services to non-EU consumers are outside French VAT, and EU B2C supplies may be reported through the One-Stop-Shop (OSS) scheme. Eligibility for 0% or no-French-VAT treatment requires documented customer identification, VAT/tax registration evidence, contracts, and payment records.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (DAU) validated through DELTA-X
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, CMR, or postal/export carrier receipt
Proof of physical exit from the EU (carrier certificate, destination customs entry, or seal evidence)
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank SWIFT credit confirmation evidencing foreign-currency repatriation
Customer's foreign tax/VAT identification number and underlying contract or order documentation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP may rigorously audit export proof, delivery terms, and foreign-exchange repatriation records. If a 0% export exemption is disallowed for missing evidence, false declaration, or fraud, the company will be assessed for unreported French VAT at 20%, plus late-payment interest under CGI Article 1727 and penalties up to 40% for bad faith (Article 1729-1) or 80% for deliberate tax fraud/concealment (Article 1729-2). Criminal prosecution under CGI Article 1741 can result in fines up to EUR 500,000 and imprisonment up to five years. Input VAT credits previously claimed in respect of the zero-rated export can be clawed back with interest and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France is France's central bank and participates in the Eurosystem. The European Central Bank sets euro-area monetary policy. The Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution (ACPR), within the Banque de France, supervises French credit institutions and certain payment and electronic-money institutions. The Direction générale du Trésor administers relevant financial and external-financial reporting rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a euro-area member with no general foreign-exchange controls restricting current-account payments, capital transfers, dividend payments, or repatriation of investment proceeds. Cross-border euro payments within the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) generally use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer where supported; other currencies and non-SEPA destinations generally use correspondent banking and SWIFT. Payments remain subject to sanctions screening, anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist-financing controls, tax rules, bank documentation requirements, and applicable reporting obligations. Dividend distributions require distributable reserves and valid corporate approvals under French company law, with withholding-tax and treaty analysis as applicable. A French SAS should maintain records supporting the commercial purpose, beneficial ownership, source of funds, and tax treatment of significant cross-border flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory requirement to repatriate or convert export proceeds into euros and no mandatory export-proceeds conversion ratio. Receipts may be retained in foreign-currency accounts, subject to bank terms, accounting and tax requirements, sanctions controls, and applicable financial reporting. There is no general statutory conversion deadline for ordinary export receipts. Banks may request invoices, contracts, shipping or service evidence, and payment-purpose information.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; Capital Escrow Account where required for incorporation or a capital increase
Operational Account; Capital Escrow Account where required for incorporation or a capital increase
Operational Account; Capital Escrow Account where required for incorporation or a capital increase
Operational Account, subject to product eligibility and underwriting
Operational Account; Capital Escrow Account where offered by the relevant entity

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High for routine euro collections and payments if the provider is an EEA-authorized payment institution or electronic-money institution permitted to provide services in France, including through valid passporting where applicable. An EMI balance is electronic money or safeguarded client funds, not a bank deposit, and generally is not covered by the French deposit-guarantee scheme. Verify the provider's authorization, French service permissions, safeguarding arrangements, account-holder name, supported currencies, transfer limits, and access to SEPA and SWIFT. Do not rely on an offshore EMI as the sole operating or capital account where counterparties, tax authorities, or the company's bank require a French or EEA credit-institution account. Stripe may support payment processing but should not be treated as a substitute for a corporate bank account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No general French statutory rule requires directors to appear physically at a bank branch. Remote onboarding may be available, but each institution determines its process and may require in-person verification, a live video interview, certified identity documents, or a French address. Non-resident directors, complex ownership chains, unusual funding sources, or elevated risk indicators commonly result in enhanced due diligence and may require physical attendance. Confirm requirements with the selected bank before incorporation funding or transaction execution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder, director, or ultimate beneficial owner; layered ownership; nominee arrangements; or inability to identify natural-person beneficial owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current group organization chart to natural-person beneficial owners; certified registry extracts and constitutional documents for each relevant entity; passports and proof of residential address; beneficial-ownership filings and declarations; director and shareholder resolutions; explanation of control rights; and French beneficial-ownership register evidence where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital funding from a third party, an unrelated jurisdiction, a high-risk source, or an account that does not match the shareholder or lender.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Subscription or shareholder-loan agreement; board and shareholder approvals; originating bank statements; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence; ownership and control records for the remitter; transfer instructions identifying the SAS and funding purpose; and supporting tax or audited financial records where appropriate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newswire activity, customers, counterparties, or payment flows appearing inconsistent with the declared financial-market information service, including unexplained high-value or rapid pass-through transactions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan and service description; website and product materials; customer and supplier contracts; sample invoices; pricing and revenue model; explanation that the company aggregates and syndicates information and does not receive, hold, transmit, or execute customer investment funds; transaction-flow diagram; and applicable regulatory-perimeter analysis.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving sanctioned persons or territories, politically exposed persons, adverse media, opaque intermediaries, or mismatched payment references.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Documented customer and counterparty screening; sanctions and PEP-screening results; contract, invoice, and service-delivery evidence; beneficial-ownership checks; payment-purpose explanation; escalation and approval records; and evidence of rejection or blocking where legally required.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Open the SAS account or, where required, a capital-deposit account with a French credit institution or other eligible depositary. Route subscribed share capital from the shareholder's own verified account to the depositary account, identifying the SAS, subscriber, and purpose as share capital or capital increase. Provide the subscription documents, incorporation or capital-increase resolutions, ownership and source-of-funds evidence, and remitter account proof. Obtain the deposit certificate and complete the release process after registration or the applicable corporate formalities. For shareholder loans, use a separate documented loan agreement, approvals, repayment terms, and accounting treatment; do not describe debt funding as equity. SEPA Credit Transfer is generally appropriate for euro transfers within SEPA; use SWIFT with accurate beneficiary, bank, and payment-purpose details for non-SEPA or non-euro transfers. The bank may request supporting documents and may delay or reject transfers pending AML, sanctions, or source-of-funds review. France does not have a universal corporate FX purpose-code regime comparable to exchange-control jurisdictions.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within SEPA, subject to bank availability and limits. Use SWIFT customer credit transfers, commonly documented through MT103-format information or its ISO 20022 successor, for non-SEPA or foreign-currency payments. Match beneficiary details and payment references to the underlying invoice, contract, or service period; retain evidence of delivery and approval. Commercial letters of credit, documentary collections, and bank guarantees may be arranged through a French bank when commercially justified, subject to credit approval, fees, and the applicable ICC rules incorporated into the instrument. For recurring supplier, payroll, tax, and treasury payments, use controlled payment files, dual authorization, beneficiary verification, sanctions screening, and reconciliation. Apply VAT, corporate-tax, withholding-tax, and transfer-pricing analysis independently of the payment rail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an authorized bank or investment firm, supported by documented underlying exposures, approved treasury limits, and appropriate accounting treatment.
Non-deliverable forwards where offered and suitable for the exposure; assess counterparty, settlement, valuation, and regulatory classification.
Foreign-exchange swaps and cross-currency swaps with an authorized counterparty, documented under appropriate master agreements and collateral terms.
Spot foreign-exchange conversions for operational receipts and payments, with execution through an authorized provider and documented pricing and approvals.

Options or other derivatives only where permitted by the company's mandate and counterparty arrangements; assess MiFID II classification, EMIR reporting and risk-mitigation duties, clearing or margin requirements where applicable, and accounting consequences.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts approval and filing (dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce – Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder approval of financial statements within 6 months of fiscal year-end; RCS filing within 1 month after approval (for a calendar-year business, approval by 30 June and filing by 31 July)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: administrative fine up to €1,500 per fiscal period; after two consecutive years of non-filing, judicial request may result in mandatory audit; persistent failure leads to RCS strike-off (radiation) and possible civil liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial owner register update (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce – Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any change in shareholding or beneficial control; annual confirmation at the ordinary general meeting no later than 6 months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file/update within 30 days: fine up to €10,000 for the legal entity and €5,000 for its legal representative; intentional concealment potentially subject to €50,000 criminal fine and imprisonment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (déclaration de résultats annuels, form 2065-SD)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For fiscal year ending 31 December, due 3 May of the following year; for non-calendar year-end, due the second business day of the third month following the close
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: 10% surcharge on the tax payable (40% after formal notice), monthly late-payment interest (0.2% per month), and a fixed administrative fine of up to €150.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local business contribution declaration and payment (cotisation foncière des entreprises – CFE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP – Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Declaration (form 1447-C) filed with the annual results declaration by the same May deadline for calendar-year companies; tax payment due by 15 December of the assessment year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment: 10% penalty, monthly interest of 0.2% on outstanding tax, and potential attachment/execution of company assets.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit (commissaire aux comptes) is mandatory for an SAS that exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds at fiscal year-end: total balance sheet €4,000,000; net turnover €8,000,000; average headcount 50. Audit also mandatory if the company controls or is controlled by a group subject to consolidated audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP – Plan Comptable Général (PCG) per Articles 123-12 to 123-23 of the French Commercial Code; IFRS applies only voluntarily for consolidated reporting and is mandatory for listed groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No separate annual UBO re-filing exists in France unless a shareholding transfer or beneficial ownership change occurs. The annual general meeting (within 6 months of year-end) must verify that the declaration on file at the RCS remains accurate; if a change has taken place, an updated declaration must be lodged with the RCS within 30 days of the triggering event.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Registre des mouvements de titres (Share Transfer Register)
Registre des procès-verbaux et décisions (Minutes Book)
Registre des décisions unilatérales du président (President's Decisions Register)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,100 – USD 2,700 per year for professional registered office and correspondent services (location-dependent; Paris metropolitan area at the higher end)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 – USD 14,000 for a small SAS close to the compulsory audit thresholds; USD 0 when audit thresholds are not met and no voluntary audit is appointed.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D tax credit (up to 30%), accelerated depreciation allowances, and targeted tax holidays for innovative investments

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 1201 - Déclaration de résultat, submitted via official portal impots.gouv.fr
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Three months following the close of the fiscal year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only French-sourced income; non-residents file for French branch or permanent establishment income
Incorporate transfer pricing adjustments and DTA relief claims
Apply 25% rate after deductions; claim any applicable credits

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 0.5% to 5% of tax due monthly, maximum 80%; willful non-compliance may result in criminal sanctions

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Obtain Tax Residency Certificate from home jurisdiction and submit application for reduced rate under applicable DTA to French tax authorities
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% to 10% depending on treaty; Interest: generally 0% or 10% per DTA

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €50 million in consolidated group revenue for Master File and Local File requirements
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France enforces economic substance requirements for tax residency and certain regimes including IP Box under DAC6 and anti-avoidance provisions

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable income or false declarations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties: fines up to 500% of evaded tax and imprisonment from 1 to 5 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for restitution, fines, and potential imprisonment; corporate veil may be pierced

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a shell company without adequate business activities in France
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to €75,000 per violation and potential company dissolution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal civil and criminal liability including jail time for fraudulent management

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare or file TP documentation or apply arm's length principle
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines ranging from €10,000 to €100,000 plus potential back taxes and interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal fines and liability for management errors

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to withhold and remit WHT on dividends, royalties, or interest paid to non-residents
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties up to 500% of unpaid WHT plus interest and possible criminal charges
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for directors who authorized or failed to comply
